$comment: WHETHER ONE PRIVATE-CONVERSATION MESSAGE MAY ALERT, WRITTEN ONCE AND ASSERTED ON EVERY PLATFORM.
A conversation's level (all / mentions / none) cannot be applied by the server at `mentions`: who a
ciphertext names is only known after decryption. So three implementations decide it - the client's
`NotificationLevelGate` and the iOS extension's `levelDecision` - and this file is the contract they
are each tested against, so the three copies cannot drift. See docs/wiki/services/chat-delivery.md,
Fields: `level` is the push's `notifLevel` (`null` = absent, the ordinary `all`); `text` is the
decrypted plaintext, `null` when the device could not read it; `me` is this account's id, `null`
when it could not be loaded. `expected`: `alert` (draw it), `alert-mention` (draw it on the
mentions channel / time-sensitive), `withhold` (Android and the client draw nothing; iOS keeps the
alert passive and soundless, since an extension cannot withhold one).
WHO READS WHICH CASE. The native paths never receive `none` as a visible frame (the server sends it
silent), so they skip `level: "none"`. The client always holds the plaintext and its own id, so it
skips `text: null` and `me: null` - the undecidable cases only a push can meet.

cases.name: ordinary frame nobody could read still alerts
mentions, naming me in upper case
mentions, my id without the token is not a mention
mentions, the mention is past the 200-character preview
mentions, own id unknown: the stated rule
